news.title: Argentina were World Cup’s most targeted team online, says FIFA report
news.lede: Argentina were the most targeted national team on social media during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, with accusations of referee favouritism, corruption and xenophobia among the main forms of abuse directed at the side, a FIFA report published on October 9 noted. The governing body’s Social Media Protection Service (SMPS) analysed more than 17.1 million posts and comments on X, Instagram, Facebook and TikTok between June 9 and July 20. Of those, 477,000 were referred for human review, with 240,000 verified as abusive. England were the second-most targeted team, followed by Spain, Brazil and Norway, the report found.

news.title: Finland beat Serbia women 3-1 in Tampere World Cup playoff
news.lede: Finland captain Ema Koivisto rose highest to meet a cross in the 28th minute in Tampere and put her side ahead against Serbia's women. Eight minutes later, Lota Lindstrom doubled the lead after a solo run, with goalkeeper Milica Kostic powerless to stop it. Finland went into halftime two goals up in the first leg of the first round of the 2027 World Cup playoff, and Serbia ended up losing 3-1. Who started for Serbia in Tampere?

news.title: Motsepe: Africa must win World Cup
news.lede: SANTA MARIA: CAF President Patrice Motsepe has challenged African football to turn its growing influence on the world stage into tangible results, declaring that the continent must win the FIFA World Cup. He made the statement yesterday during the second day of the CAF Strategy Conference in Santa Maria, Sal Island, Cabo Verde. news.title: England gains edge over Greece in FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 play-offs
news.lede: REUTERS REUTERS https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/8gfofh/article71566998.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/2026-10-09T182629Z_1100204993_UP1EMA91F84J8_RTRMADP_3_SOCCER-WORLDCUP-GRC-ENG.JPG STEFANOS RAPANIS Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2027 - Play Off - Semi Final - First Leg - Greece v England - Pankritio Stadium, Heraklion, Greece - October 9, 2026 England's Alessia Russo celebrates scoring their third goal with teammates REUTERS/Stefanos Rapanis Kallisti Brouksair pulled one back for the host, giving Greece a glimmer of hope ahead of Tuesday’s return leg in Leicester against the 2023 World Cup runner-up. PARIS England secured a 3-1 win away to Greece on Friday in the first leg of their 2027 Women’s World Cup play-off. Georgia Stanway gave the Lionesses a first-half lead in Crete before Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo put England firmly in control with two more goals after the break.

news.title: Lionesses take control of World Cup playoff tie but unfancied Greece still in fight
news.lede: World Cup qualifying playoff: Greece 1-3 England. Stanway, Le Tissier and Russo on target. Sarina Wiegman said she wanted to see a bit more from her side after their fairly underwhelming performance against a hugely unfancied Greek side, despite securing a valuable first-leg victory in their Women’s World Cup playoff tie. Georgia Stanway’s neat finish, Maya Le Tissier’s first England goal and Alessia Russo’s low strike were enough to give England control but a Kallisti Brouksair goal for Greece means that the tie is not definitively over, going into Tuesday’s second leg, and Wiegman acknowledged that England had been “a bit sloppy” at times.
